newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-REAL FANS CELEBRATE WITH STREET PARTY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-REAL FANS CELEBRATE WITH STREET PARTY.

text.p: Nearly a million Real Madrid fans celebrated their team's 27th league title in the streets of the Spanish capital until the early hours of Sunday morning.
But the Real players abandoned their own festivities after being told of the death of the young son of the club doctor in a household accident.
Real, needing one point to clinch the title, played their best game of the season to beat reigning champions Atletico 3-1 on Saturday.
Atletico coach Radomir Antic and Bobby Robson, coach of second-placed Barcelona, praised Real and their coach Fabio Capello, who confirmed after the game he was returning to AC Milan next season.
"We had the Cup and the European Cup Winners' Cup (to play), they didn't...and they took advantage of it," said Robson.
Tenerife coach Jupp Heynckes would likely take over at the Bernabeu stadium, according to Real president Lorenzo Sanz.
Even before the final whistle supporters were gathering at the Cibeles fountain, the traditional centre of Real victory celebrations.
Spanish police estimate 800,000 fans celebrated in the streets and 350,000 cheered the players when they climbed the fountain, which had been sealed off and drained as a security precaution.
The players moved on to a victory dinner after climbing Cibeles but cut short their celebrations when news of the tragedy reached them in the early hours of Sunday morning.

Alvaro, the six-year-old son of Alfonso del Corral, died from injuries sustained when he was hit by a garage door at his home. Many of the players and club officials attended his funeral service on Sunday afternoon.
Some 140 people needed medical treatment during the night and a 30-year-old man was in a critical condition after suffering a heart attack during the celebrations.
